claim: The PeerNotifier interface's doc comment confirms file-based peer discovery is a real, named alternative fed into the same sink as the Kubernetes reconciler, mirroring the file-vs-k8s duality already established for endpoint discovery.
stance_target: feasibility of a custom non-k8s PeerDiscovery plugin for cross-replica state sync
quoted_support: It mirrors DiscoveryNotifier: the k8s reconciler and any file-based discovery feed the same sink.

claim: PeerStore is intentionally kept separate from the endpoint Datastore because peers and endpoints have different consumers (cross-replica syncer vs. scheduler) and different lifecycles, with endpoints explicitly bound to the InferencePool (a Kubernetes CRD) even in an architecture that otherwise decouples peer tracking from Kubernetes.
stance_target: how deeply InferencePool (a k8s-specific CRD) is embedded in the endpoint lifecycle even under a pluggable discovery architecture
quoted_support: endpoints and peers have different consumers (scheduler vs. cross-replica syncer) and different lifecycles (bound to the InferencePool vs. the EPP deployment)

claim: No built-in PeerDiscovery implementation (neither a Kubernetes nor a file-based one) ships in llm-d-router's datalayer interface package itself -- only the interface is defined, consistent with peer-discovery.md's finding that no built-in plugin type is named anywhere in the docs.
quoted_support: PeerDiscovery discovers peer EPP replicas and drives their lifecycle through a PeerNotifier. Implementations are registered in the plugin registry and selected via EndpointPickerConfig.dataLayer.discovery.peers.pluginRef.
